label: Requests for founders
title: I came to the US with nothing and built companies for immigrants. Now I want to build the next ones with you.
intro: Hey, I'm Siam. Over fifteen years I've guided more than two hundred thousand students abroad, helped immigrants earn millions in US salaries, and run a fund for the ones who made it. Along the way I kept finding problems that deserve a company and don't have one.
These are those openings. Pick one, or bring yours. Tell me what you're great at — building or selling — and we put in the rest: design, engineering or distribution, and my time.

pillars.v: Sixty ideas at launch, each a one-pager on purpose, chosen from a library of nearly two thousand by the demand behind them and by whether one of our companies already owns the audience. The first one-pagers are live; the rest are being written. The full research is shared once we're talking.
Every founder is missing a leg. Builders lack distribution; sellers lack a product. We map what you don't have and bring it — design always, and either the engineering or the go-to-market.
Co-founder, equity. We're not an agency and we're not an accelerator. We're the partner who already has the team, the audience and the operating history.

triadIntro: Every company needs all three. We are the hipster — design, brand, the customer's experience — on every idea. Then we add whichever of the other two you don't bring.

triad.name: Hacker
triad.who: You, if you're the Builder. Us, if you're not.

triad.name: Hipster
triad.what: Design, brand, experience — the Algorizin design system on day one.

triad.name: Hustler
triad.who: You, if you're the Hustler. Us, if you're not.
triad.what: Sales, content, distribution, the first customers.

whoIntro: Immigrant founders, solo founders ideally. International students and international founders get preference — I've been one, I've built for hundreds of thousands of them, and I know the constraints. Two profiles, and you only need to be one.

icps.name: The Builder
icps.line: A 10× engineer who ships with AI tools at rocket speed and cares how it feels to use.
you: Build end to end — backend, frontend, data, deploy — alone if you have to
Fluent with today's AI coding tools; a working product in weeks, not quarters
Product-minded: you sweat the user experience, not just the architecture
Have shipped something real, even if nobody bought it
we: Design — every screen, in a system that already exists
Distribution — the customers, communities and channels our companies already reach
The first ten conversations, opened for you

icps.name: The Hustler
icps.line: A seller or a creator who can move people — and ideally already has an audience.
you: Can sell anything to anyone, and prove it with a pipeline you've run
Or: make content people actually consume, with a distribution you already own
Live inside a customer community and speak its language
Comfortable charging money from day one
we: Design — every screen, in a system that already exists
Engineering — Algorizin's team builds the product to your spec
The operating playbook from companies that already sell to this audience

ideasIntro: Sixty to start, more as we write them. They follow one life in three stages — study, build, manage — and each stage has a company of ours behind it that already reaches the people it serves. Titles are listed now; each one-pager goes live as it's written. Tap a stage.

help.v: A complete design system and the people who use it. Your product looks finished before it is.
Algorizin's delivery team for the MVP when the founder is the seller.
HigherStudyAbroad's student community, Algorizin's clients, XenosWealth's members — whichever the idea needs.
Fifteen years of running companies in these exact markets, and the mistakes already made.
Me, weekly, for as long as it takes to find product-market fit.

steps.k: Pick an idea, or bring yours
steps.v: Any one-pager above, or something you've seen that we haven't.
Thirty minutes. Builder or Hustler, what you've shipped or sold, where you are in the world.
I say plainly what you're missing and what we'd put in.
Design in week one. A product or a pipeline by week twelve. Then we decide together whether it's a company.

closeText: Thirty minutes, no deck needed. Bring what you've built or sold and the idea you can't stop thinking about.
footer: Open Ideas is run by Siam Hossain and Algorizin, Inc. Ideas are shared as one-pagers on purpose; the research behind each is shared with people we start working with.
